takeaway: Hyperthyroidism causes tremor, tachycardia, low serum cholesterol and hyperreflexia; the opposite findings point to hypothyroidism.

question.text: Typical physical and laboratory findings in hyperthyroidism include which of the following?
question.say: Typical physical and laboratory findings in hyperthyroidism include which of the following?

lines.text: His thyroid is on fire: hyperthyroidism.
lines.say: Look at his neck. The thyroid is on fire. This man has hyperthyroidism.

lines.text: His hand shakes and the tea spills: tremor.
lines.say: His hand shakes so much that the tea spills from the glass. That is tremor.
(laugh) And the other hand is trembling too.
Inside, his heart beats a fast drum. That is tachycardia.

lines.text: Low serum cholesterol and hyperreflexia also fit.
lines.say: Hyperthyroidism also brings a low serum cholesterol and brisk reflexes, called hyperreflexia.

lines.text: The other options are classical findings of hypothyroidism.
lines.say: All the other options are classical findings of hypothyroidism, the opposite state.

lines.text: Remember: a hot thyroid shakes the hands: tremor.
lines.say: Remember: an overactive thyroid shakes the hands. Tremor is a typical finding in hyperthyroidism.
